issues.label: Juvenile court jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm subject-matter and personal jurisdiction over a delinquency and juvenile-traffic matter.

issues.label: Proper complaint/citation filing
issues.why: Court must ensure complaints and the traffic citation were properly filed, sworn, and complied with Juvenile Rules and local practice.

issues.label: Statutory elements mapping
issues.why: Court must map each delinquency count to the adult offense elements and required proof beyond a reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Effect of dismissed charges
issues.why: Court must ensure dismissed burglary/RSP counts do not prejudice remaining adjudications or taint evidence rulings.

issues.label: Jaywalking ordinance applicability
issues.why: Court must determine CMC 506.46 applied at the location and circumstances of the crossing.

issues.label: Identity of jaywalking location
issues.why: Court must resolve whether the inconsistent addresses undermine proof of where the jaywalking occurred.

issues.label: Refiling citation legality
issues.why: Court must address whether dismissal/refiling of the jaywalking citation was timely and procedurally proper.

issues.label: Double jeopardy on refiling
issues.why: Court must determine whether jeopardy attached to the first jaywalking filing such that refiling was barred.

issues.label: Speedy trial/time limits
issues.why: Court must consider juvenile speedy-trial/time-limit rules for the refiled citation and delinquency counts.

issues.label: Due process notice
issues.why: Court must ensure K.J. had adequate notice of the time, place, and conduct alleged for each offense.

issues.label: Suppression standing/privacy
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J. had a reasonable expectation of privacy in the apartment/closet/lunchbox searched.

issues.label: Stop vs seizure timing
issues.why: Court must determine when any Fourth Amendment seizure occurred (approach, commands, chase, or capture).

issues.label: Reasonable suspicion for stop
issues.why: Court must decide if officers had reasonable suspicion to detain based on observed jaywalking and other factors.

issues.label: Probable cause for jaywalking stop
issues.why: Court must decide whether a completed minor offense provided authority for the attempted stop/citation.

issues.label: Officer-observation requirement
issues.why: Court must decide whether an officer may stop/cite for jaywalking based on another officer’s observation (collective knowledge).

issues.label: Collective knowledge doctrine
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether Davis’s report could be imputed to the stopping officers for RS/PC.

issues.label: Credibility at suppression
issues.why: Court must resolve witness credibility and factual disputes affecting the legality of the encounter.

issues.label: High-crime area weight
issues.why: Court must determine how much weight to give “high crime area” as a factor in reasonable suspicion.

issues.label: Gun-carry indicators relevance
issues.why: Court must assess whether waist-grab behavior and crossbody bag add articulable suspicion of a weapon.

issues.label: Pretextual enforcement limits
issues.why: Court must decide whether the jaywalking basis was lawful even if officers’ real motive was gun investigation.

issues.label: Flight as suspicion/probable cause
issues.why: Court must analyze whether unprovoked flight after a lawful/consensual encounter supports RS or PC.

issues.label: Flight after unlawful attempt
issues.why: Court must decide whether flight from an unlawful attempted stop can create lawful grounds for detention/arrest.

issues.label: Obstruction legal standard
issues.why: Court must apply R.C. 2921.31: whether K.J. acted with purpose and actually hampered/impaired official duties.

issues.label: Lawful duty requirement
issues.why: Court must determine whether officers were performing a lawful duty when K.J. ran (a prerequisite for obstruction).

issues.label: Mere flight vs obstruction
issues.why: Court must decide whether running alone, without more, constitutes obstruction under Ohio law.

issues.label: Probable cause to arrest
issues.why: Court must decide whether facts at the time of custody established PC to arrest for obstruction or any other offense.

issues.label: Show of authority seizure
issues.why: Court must decide whether threats to tase/commands to stop created a seizure absent submission.

issues.label: Hot pursuit entry legality
issues.why: Court must determine whether entry/following into a residence area was justified (exigent circumstances/hot pursuit) and for what offense.

issues.label: Warrant requirement exceptions
issues.why: Court must analyze whether any warrantless entry/search was justified by consent, exigency, protective sweep, or other exceptions.

issues.label: Third-party consent
issues.why: Court must determine who controlled the apartment and whether valid consent was obtained for the search.

issues.label: Scope of consent/search
issues.why: Court must decide whether searching a utility closet and lunchbox stayed within any consent or exception scope.

issues.label: Protective sweep limits
issues.why: Court must assess whether any sweep was permissible and whether the gun’s discovery exceeded sweep bounds.

issues.label: Plain view doctrine
issues.why: Court must decide if the gun was in plain view or required opening/inspection of a container, affecting admissibility.

issues.label: Search incident to arrest
issues.why: Court must determine whether any search was justified as incident to arrest and its permissible scope/location.

issues.label: Detention duration reasonableness
issues.why: Court must assess whether holding perimeter for 20–30 minutes before exit was reasonable under the Fourth Amendment.

issues.label: Seizure of bag evidence
issues.why: Court must determine whether the crossbody bag was lawfully seized and whether its location suggests abandonment.

issues.label: Marijuana evidence relevance
issues.why: Court must consider whether marijuana evidence was admissible or unduly prejudicial to weapon/tampering charges.

issues.label: Fruit of poisonous tree
issues.why: Court must decide whether the gun and statements must be suppressed as fruits of an unlawful stop/arrest/search.

issues.label: Attenuation/independent source
issues.why: Court must determine if any intervening circumstances or independent source purged any taint.

issues.label: Inevitable discovery
issues.why: Court must consider whether the gun would have been discovered lawfully regardless of any illegality.

issues.label: Suppression ruling legal framing
issues.why: Court must assess whether the court applied correct standards (Terry vs PC) and correct burden allocation.

issues.label: Miranda compliance
issues.why: Court must determine whether K.J.’s custodial statements were preceded by proper Miranda warnings and waiver.

issues.label: Voluntariness of confession
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J.’s statement was voluntary under the totality of circumstances for a juvenile.

issues.label: Juvenile interrogation safeguards
issues.why: Court must consider age, comprehension, and any statutory/constitutional juvenile protections during questioning.

issues.label: Corroboration of confession
issues.why: Court must determine whether K.J.’s admissions were sufficiently corroborated by independent evidence of the charged acts.

issues.label: Concealed weapon elements
issues.why: Court must decide whether evidence proved K.J. knowingly had a deadly weapon concealed on his person/ready at hand.

issues.label: Definition of concealed/ready at hand
issues.why: Court must determine whether placement in a crossbody bag or elsewhere satisfies concealment and accessibility standards.

issues.label: Possession type (actual/constructive)
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J. had actual or constructive possession of the firearm found in the closet.

issues.label: Operability of firearm
issues.why: Court must confirm the firearm was operable or readily convertible as required for the weapon offense.

issues.label: Knowledge/mental state weapon
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J. knowingly carried the firearm, including based on his statements and circumstances.

issues.label: Tampering elements
issues.why: Court must decide whether K.J. altered/destroyed/concealed evidence with purpose to impair its value or availability.

issues.label: Pending/likely investigation
issues.why: Court must decide whether an official proceeding/investigation was in progress or likely when the concealment occurred.

issues.label: Purpose to impair evidence
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether hiding the gun in a closet/lunchbox was done with the required intent.

issues.label: Temporal nexus for tampering
issues.why: Court must determine whether tampering occurred after awareness of police pursuit/stop, not merely prior possession.

issues.label: Obstruction evidence sufficiency
issues.why: Court must decide whether the State proved beyond a reasonable doubt the act and impairment elements of obstruction.

issues.label: Jaywalking proof burden
issues.why: Court must decide whether evidence showed beyond a reasonable doubt K.J. crossed outside a crosswalk as charged.

issues.label: Citation officer knowledge
issues.why: Court must consider whether issuing officer’s lack of personal observation affects proof or admissibility at trial.

issues.label: Inconsistent address impact
issues.why: Court must decide whether address discrepancies create reasonable doubt or merely clerical variance.

issues.label: Variance/amendment issues
issues.why: Court must determine whether any variance between pleading and proof was material and prejudiced K.J.

issues.label: Manifest weight review
issues.why: Court must evaluate credibility and conflicts in evidence on jaywalking for weight of the evidence.

issues.label: Sufficiency review standard
issues.why: Court must apply the correct legal standard when reviewing sufficiency for each adjudication.

issues.label: Evidence admissibility at trial
issues.why: Court must ensure the gun, DNA, and other exhibits were properly authenticated and admitted under Evidence Rules.

issues.label: DNA evidence foundation
issues.why: Court must determine whether DNA collection/testing had proper chain of custody and scientific reliability.

issues.label: Fourth Amendment DNA seizure
issues.why: Court must consider whether collecting K.J.’s DNA was lawful (consent, warrant, incident to lawful arrest, or statute).

issues.label: Chain of custody firearm
issues.why: Court must confirm the gun’s chain of custody supports admission and weight of evidence.

issues.label: Hearsay and radio dispatch
issues.why: Court must decide proper use of radio communications (effect on listener vs truth) and any Confrontation issues.

issues.label: Confrontation clause considerations
issues.why: Court must ensure testimonial statements were subject to cross-examination where required.

issues.label: Juvenile adjudication rights
issues.why: Court must ensure K.J. received due process rights applicable in juvenile delinquency (counsel, confrontation, proof BRD).

issues.label: Separate adjudication vs disposition
issues.why: Court must ensure adjudication findings preceded disposition and were supported by written/journalized entries.

issues.label: Merger/allied offenses
issues.why: Court must consider whether concealed weapon and tampering (or obstruction) are allied offenses for disposition purposes.

issues.label: Disposition statutory authority
issues.why: Court must ensure the imposed DYS commitment/suspension and conditions are authorized for the offense levels and juvenile status.

issues.label: Commitment length legality
issues.why: Court must confirm any DYS commitment “until 21” complies with statutory maximums for the offenses and juvenile category.

issues.label: Suspended commitment conditions
issues.why: Court must ensure treatment/probation conditions are reasonable, specific, and related to rehabilitation and public safety.

issues.label: Stay-away order validity
issues.why: Court must confirm the no-contact/stay-away condition is lawful, supported by the record, and not overbroad.

issues.label: Costs and indigency findings
issues.why: Court must ensure proper findings/process for remitting costs based on indigency.

issues.label: Journalization and finality
issues.why: Court must ensure suppression, adjudication, and disposition orders were properly journalized and final for appeal.

issues.label: Standard of review on appeal
issues.why: Court must apply the correct standards for suppression (mixed questions), sufficiency (de novo), and manifest weight (deference).
